behavior: A social, diurnal ground forager that often gathers in flocks, walking or running with a head-bobbing motion while pecking for seeds and fruit. Flight is strong, steady, and direct. Courting birds bow, coo, inflate the throat, and strut; both parents incubate and feed the young.
field_marks: Stocky body with a small head and short legs
Typical plumage blue-gray, though feral birds vary widely
Two bold black bars across the folded wing
Glossy green-to-purple iridescence on the neck
Straight grayish bill with a pale, fleshy cere
Broad, rounded tail with a dark terminal band
habitat: Rocky cliffs and ledges, open fields, farmland, towns, and other built environments. Nests occupy sheltered crevices, ledges, and recesses in cliffs or structures.
